$comment: Machine-readable record of every Higgsfield generation for NEVAMIS. A row exists BEFORE the credit is spent, and is updated with the outcome after. This file must allow a later reproduction of any asset. Budget is finite: 1,210 credits, unlim off, every generation paid.
line: The work moves. You still decide.

budget.plan: 7 video shots total (S05/S06/S07/S10/S12 are composited type and cost nothing). ~378 credits for one attempt each at 54, leaving real headroom for selection and retries. Mobile and social variants are ffmpeg derivations of the 1080p master, not extra generations.

costPerGeneration.soul_2 image (2k): 0.12 credits — preflighted with get_cost, confirmed by balance delta
costPerGeneration.method: generate_image/generate_video accept get_cost:true, which prices a job without submitting it. Used before every spend; no calibration-by-spending was necessary.

budget.policy: Still before video, always: a rejected still costs a fraction of a rejected clip. Identity locked once and reused. No generation without a row here first.

identityLocks.objective: Lock the owner-operator's identity so every shot containing him is the same man: early 50s, electrical contractor, grey at the temples, worn hands, no blazer. Competent, never comic, never flustered.
identityLocks.modelReason: Soul 2.0 issues a soul_id for personalised generation, which is the mechanism for character consistency across later shots.
identityLocks.prompt: Photographic portrait of a 52-year-old Canadian electrical contractor in an unfinished basement. Weathered face, grey at the temples, three-day stubble, calm and focused. Worn navy work shirt with sleeves rolled, scuffed tool belt. Hands show real work. Lit by a single warm worklamp from frame left, deep shadow falloff behind him, cool ambient fill. Shallow depth of field, 50mm, fine film grain, deep neutral background. Documentary realism, not a stock portrait.
identityLocks.negative: smiling at camera, corporate headshot, blazer, hard hat cliche, clean hands, studio backdrop, robot, hologram, HUD, neon, purple gradient, lens flare, plastic skin, beauty retouching
identityLocks.finalUse: Character reference passed to every subsequent Ray shot.
identityLocks.selectedFrom: ref-ray-v3.png (batch 1, job 21b7f4b7-2638-4d05-998a-cba1a4d177c3), cropped to face-only 560x600 at offset 690,15
identityLocks.selectionReason: Correct age read (early 50s), grey temples and beard, weathered and calm, warm key from frame left with the specified hard falloff. Best identity match of eight.

rejections.reason: Bald rather than grey at the temples; posed with hands clasped, reading as waiting rather than working; gibberish text on a paper at frame left, which is an explicit rejection criterion.
Red chest patch carrying clear gibberish lettering. Also reads mid-40s and the background is lit cool, which inverts the warm-for-people rule.
Not selected; superseded by v3 on age and lighting.
Saturated workwear branding present despite an explicit no-logo instruction.
Best posture of the second batch — looking down at his hands, genuinely mid-work — but reads early 60s rather than early 50s, and carries YELLOW chest embroidery that a red-only screen missed.

lessons: Soul 2.0 reliably invents workwear branding on work shirts, and a no-logo instruction in the prompt does not stop it. Do not fight it prompt-side.
An identity lock needs a FACE, not a torso. Cropping above the chest removes every wardrobe brand mark deterministically and costs nothing.
My first branding screen tested for saturated RED and passed an image whose logo was YELLOW. The corrected screen tests for any strongly saturated non-skin hue.
An earlier version of that screen counted 38,209 red pixels that were warm-lit SKIN. A detector has to be checked against a known case before its verdict is trusted.

identityLocks.objective: Lock the environment and lighting of the panel scene so S01, S02 and S03 are continuous.
identityLocks.modelReason: Highest photoreal quality with 4K output; used as the environment plate and lighting reference.
identityLocks.prompt: Unfinished residential basement, open electrical breaker panel on a stud wall, cover off, breakers and copper visible. A single warm worklamp clamped to a joist throws hard light across the panel; the rest of the room falls into deep blue-black shadow. Concrete floor, exposed joists, a step ladder just in frame. No people. Cinematic, 35mm, shallow depth of field, fine grain, realistic and code-plausible wiring.
identityLocks.negative: impossible wiring, glowing wires, sparks, neon, server room, data centre, holographic overlay, sci-fi, cables that go nowhere, text, signage, logos
identityLocks.finalUse: Start frame for S01 and lighting reference for S02/S03.

shots.objective: Open on competence. Both hands on the work — the honest reason he cannot answer.
shots.modelReason: Accepts start_image and end_image plus image references; macro motion needs frame control more than genre character.
shots.prompt: Extreme close-up: a gloved hand seats a breaker into an open panel with a torque screwdriver, deliberate and unhurried. Warm worklamp from frame left, deep shadow behind. Very slow push in. Shallow depth of field, fine film grain.
shots.negative: sparks, glowing wires, robot hand, prosthetic, extra fingers, malformed hand, text, UI, hologram, neon
shots.finalUse: Film beat 1 and the first segment of HERO-LOOP.

shots.objective: The call arrives and is not answered. The buzz carries the tension.
shots.prompt: Close-up of a phone in the chest pocket of a worn navy work shirt, screen upward, buzzing faintly against the fabric. The man does not look down; his attention stays on the work off-frame. Warm worklamp, cool shadow, very shallow depth of field, fine grain.
shots.negative: notification bubbles, cartoon UI, readable text on screen, glowing screen halo, hologram, neon
shots.finalUse: Film beat 2 and the second segment of HERO-LOOP.

shots.objective: NEVAMIS answers. Shown as the van's interior light rising at dusk, never as a screen.
shots.modelReason: Camera character and colour matter more than identity here; no face in frame.
shots.cameraMotion: slow lateral track, left to right
shots.prompt: A tradesman's work van parked on a suburban driveway at dusk, rear doors closed. The interior dome light comes up softly, glowing through the windows. Cool blue evening ambience, one warm interior source. Slow lateral camera track. Cinematic, shallow depth of field, fine grain.
shots.negative: logos, signage, readable text, brand names, neon, sci-fi, holographic, flying vehicle, futuristic car
shots.finalUse: Film beat 3, HERO-LOOP tail, and PROOF-01 still.

shots.objective: The thesis frame: warm practical and cool screen in one shot. The summary reaches him without stopping him.
shots.prompt: Night, suburban driveway. A contractor in his early fifties closes the rear doors of a work van. He glances at the phone in his hand; its cool screen light falls across his face while warm sodium street light rims him from behind. He reads for barely two seconds and keeps walking. Cinematic, shallow depth of field, fine grain.
shots.negative: readable UI text, notification bubbles, smiling at camera, robot, hologram, neon, lens flare
shots.finalUse: Film beat 8 and PROOF-02. Reserved warm-plus-cool frame from the visual bible.

shots.objective: The campaign line made literal. One tap, phone face-down, back to dinner.
shots.prompt: A warm domestic kitchen at night. A contractor in his early fifties sits at a dinner table with family; ordinary evening life around him. A phone lies face-up on the table showing a single line. He reaches over, taps once, turns the phone face-down and returns to the meal. Warm practical light, natural and unposed. Cinematic, shallow depth of field, fine grain.
shots.negative: readable UI text, staged family portrait, smiling at camera, stock photo warmth, robot, hologram, neon

compositedNotGenerated.$comment: These beats are type on black, built in ffmpeg from the real product's typography. They cost no credits and are the most credible seconds in the film precisely because no model renders their text.
